scope: Planning only — no dataset is modified, merged, or deleted by this file. Extends (does not duplicate) audit/dataset-mapping.json (Phase 2A), which used a different, coarser vocabulary (keep/merge/split/derived/computed/deprecated). This file resolves each dataset into exactly one of the six transition states the Phase 2B brief specifies, including resolving two judgment calls Phase 2A explicitly left open.

transitionStateDefinitions.retain: Continues operating essentially unchanged after migration — either because it's out of Name Entity scope, or because it's the correct long-term ownership point for its data under the canonical model too.
transitionStateDefinitions.merge: Its rows are folded into canonical entity records; the file's role as a standalone dataset ends once folded.
transitionStateDefinitions.reference: Remains a separate, small lookup table that canonical records point to rather than duplicate.
transitionStateDefinitions.replace: Its ROLE (not just its data) is superseded by a structurally different canonical mechanism — distinct from 'merge', where the data moves but the surrounding pattern doesn't fundamentally change.
transitionStateDefinitions.parallel: Should run alongside the canonical model for a validation period before full cutover, because it is foundational enough (or its consumers numerous enough) that an abrupt cutover is the higher-risk path.
transitionStateDefinitions.archive-after-validation: A read-only retention candidate — kept available for audit/rollback purposes until a validation step confirms it is safe to set aside, then archived (not deleted).

datasets.currentPurpose: Base identity record every other dataset joins against by name_id.
datasets.rationale: The most heavily-relied-upon file in the graph (universal prerequisite per audit/migration-dependency-graph.json). An abrupt cutover risks breaking every generator simultaneously; running it alongside the canonical identity domain during the wave-1 validation checkpoint (see docs/CANONICAL_MIGRATION_PLAN.md) is the lower-risk path.

datasets.currentPurpose: Overlay of names.json with origin_cluster/origin_confidence added, produced by merging data/origin-overrides.json.
datasets.rationale: Classified 'replace' rather than 'merge' because the canonical model doesn't just relocate this file's data — it eliminates the overlay PATTERN entirely (one record, not a base file plus a derived overlay file). This is the direct structural fix for the origin-dual-file-split finding (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json): once origin.*/language.* are native canonical fields, there is no second file left to accidentally not read.

datasets.currentPurpose: Adds slug, phonetic_code, spelling_variants[], length, syllable_estimate, and unused meaning_source/origin_source/confidence_score columns.
datasets.canonicalDestination: identity.slug, pronunciation.syllableCount / pronunciation.ipa (candidate), variants.spellingVariants[] (duplicate — see data/variants.json entry), citations.sources[] (via its unused columns)
datasets.rationale: Its spelling_variants[] column is a confirmed 100% duplicate of data/variants.json (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json, exhaustively verified) — deduplicated as part of this merge, not carried forward as a second copy.
Straightforward fold into an array field; no redundancy or inconsistency found for this dataset.

datasets.currentPurpose: Hand-curated origin/language research input (top-300-name scope per its own header comment).
datasets.rationale: Remains the correct place to author new origin research under the canonical model too (docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md, 'Ownership rules', curated-input ownership). What changes is that its merge target becomes the canonical record directly, not an intermediate overlay file.

datasets.canonicalDestination: Out of Name Entity scope entirely.
datasets.rationale: Unaffected by this migration — belongs to a future Surname Entity schema not yet defined (Phase 2A, 'Domain boundaries').

datasets.canonicalDestination: None — presentation layer, not canonical knowledge.
datasets.rationale: Untouched by a knowledge migration by design (docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md, 'Separation of canonical knowledge vs presentation').

datasets.currentPurpose: Closed, curated set of 27 cross-linguistic equivalent-name anchors.
datasets.rationale: Resolves the open judgment call Phase 2A explicitly left unresolved (audit/dataset-mapping.json: 'a judgment call for a future migration-planning phase'). Decided merge, not reference/retain, because at 27 rows the duplication cost of keeping it separate exceeds the cost of folding it into each anchor's own entity record, and because relatedNames.equivalents[] is already defined per-entity in schemas/name-entity.schema.json, not as a shared lookup table.

datasets.currentPurpose: Rule-based scoring factors/patterns for surname compatibility.
datasets.canonicalDestination: Configures relationships.surnameCompatibility[].score computation; not itself entity data.
datasets.rationale: A scoring ruleset, not knowledge about any entity — continues to exist as configuration a canonical-model-aware scoring function reads, per audit/dataset-mapping.json status 'computed'.

Confirmed to have zero live consumers today (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json compare-page-orphaned-dataset) — this merge is lower-urgency than others, since no generator currently depends on this file's content reaching a page.

datasets.currentPurpose: Prose-variant pool (intended purpose only — never wired to a renderer).
datasets.rationale: Confirmed by Phase 1B's exhaustive script-reference scan to be read by zero scripts in the repository. The clearest archive candidate in the entire dataset inventory — retained read-only pending a validation step (see docs/CANONICAL_MIGRATION_PLAN.md validation checkpoints) confirming no undiscovered consumer exists, rather than archived unilaterally by this planning phase.

datasets.currentPurpose: The one real source of per-country, per-year ranking data.
datasets.rationale: Direct fold; this is the source both country-differentials.json and regional-trend-acceleration.json independently derive from — merging it first is the natural sequencing (matches migration wave 2).
Merging a 5-row table into every one of 3,697 entity records would itself reintroduce duplication of the kind this migration is designed to remove — stays a shared reference table.
Direct fold; a real, live-consumed dataset (scripts/generate-trends-page.js), unlike country-differentials.json.

datasets.canonicalDestination: Out of Name Entity scope entirely.
datasets.rationale: Same status as data/last-names.json — a future Surname Entity concern.

Confirmed 100% duplicate of data/normalized-names.json's spelling_variants[] column across all 3,697 names (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json) — the lowest-risk merge in this entire map, since the two candidate sources already agree exactly.

notes: 19 datasets covered, matching the count established in Phase 1A (audit/datasets.json) and re-confirmed in Phase 2A (audit/dataset-mapping.json).
No dataset is marked for deletion anywhere in this file — 'archive-after-validation' is the strongest disposition used, and it is explicitly retention-then-archive, not removal.
